question.text: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes OTC derivatives from exchange-traded derivatives?

answer.text: OTC derivatives are non-standard and carry counterparty risk, while exchange-traded derivatives are standardized and settled through a clearing corporation
OTC derivatives are more liquid than exchange-traded derivatives
OTC derivatives are regulated by SEBI while exchange-traded derivatives are unregulated
OTC derivatives require margin deposits while exchange-traded derivatives do not

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 198, OTC derivatives are non-standard and depend on counterparty trust, while exchange-traded derivatives are standard contracts settled through a clearing corporation. Per page 200, futures clearing corporations collect margins and eliminate counterparty risk. The Trap: The other options invert or fabricate the distinction — claiming OTC is more liquid, only OTC is regulated, or only OTC requires margins — none of which is supported by the source pages. Note: The defining contrast supported by pages 198-200 is standardisation and clearing-corporation settlement (exchange-traded) versus non-standard, counterparty-dependent terms (OTC).
